_comment: Canonical 18Dragon privates data master. Tool-agnostic source of truth for the 30 private companies; docs/privates-roster.md is the human-readable companion. This is NOT the 18xxMaker privates schema — it is a custom 18Dragon schema (two-sided cards, players_required gating, class badge, function_label vs name). A renderer (18xxMaker or an alternative, decided in C42) consumes this.

schema.name: In-game (flavor) title.
schema.function_label: Top-band label — what the card does, in a few words.
schema.class: minor | major | minor-major — who may buy it into a company.
schema.badge: green (a minor may buy in) | red (majors only) — derived from class.
schema.phase: Earliest phase the private may be bought into a company.
schema.player_revenue: gp paid to the owning player each OR.
schema.company_revenue: gp paid to the owning company (0 = none / ability only).
schema.cadence: one-time | each-or | ongoing | null — the ability's timing (blank for trains).
schema.players_required: 3 | 4 | 5 — minimum player count; card removed below it (PRD 6.3).
schema.reverse: What the company-owned side shows (train card / marker / rules text).
schema.source: Origin / rules lineage; notes deliberate divergences.
schema.extra: Card-specific structured fields (region, bid_box, discount, toll, etc.).

privates.name: Eldrok Phlogiston Werk
privates.reverse: the 5P train card (flip, not exchanged — no train taken from supply)
privates.source: PRD 4.3 + 1822PNW P1 'Olympian Hiawatha' (matches PNW: a 5-train is the first non-rusting train, so a 'normal' 5-train is permanent by nature — no divergence).
privates.rules_text: Permanent 5-train (5P). Never rusts. Counts against the train limit. Acquiring it is an acquisition action, so a company may acquire it even at train limit; it must then discard any trains held in excess of the limit.

extra.flavor: The dwarves of Brekheim who invented the phlogiston engine; Brekheim is flavor only.

privates.name: The Ironhaul
privates.rules_text: Permanent 2-Train. The 2P-train is a permanent 2-train. It is a 'special train.' It cannot be sold to another company. It does not count against the train limit. It does not count as a train for the purpose of mandatory train ownership and purchase. A company cannot own more than one special train. Dividends can be separated from other trains and may be split, paid in full, or retained. Does not close.

privates.name: Merger Negotiations
privates.source: 18Dragon original (ties to the C13 merger mechanic)
privates.rules_text: While owned by a minor, the company may close this private to initiate a merger with another minor company, even with no connecting track. If bought into a major it closes immediately for no effect (so a player who cannot use it is not stuck with a dead certificate).

privates.name: Phlogiston Mine
privates.rules_text: The owning company may close this private to place a +30 token on any mountain hex; any train running through that hex gains +30.

privates.name: The Firebox
privates.rules_text: May be attached to a 2-7 train; that train may make 1 additional stop.

privates.name: The Emberwain
privates.rules_text: May be attached to a 2-7 train; that train may make 1 additional stop.

privates.name: Wands Delivery
privates.rules_text: When bought into a company, place a $30 token in any city not in Verantum. Any train that includes both Verantia and that city gains +30.

privates.name: Verantum Recolonization
privates.rules_text: The owning company may close this private to upgrade a Verantum dit to a city of the same color (yellow if no track has been laid) and place an Exchange token there at no cost. This counts as the company's track lay.

privates.name: Brekheim Locomotive Corporation
privates.rules_text: When bought into a company, that company may immediately place an exchange token in Brekheim, even if there is no slot available.

privates.name: Dustfall Company
privates.rules_text: Allows the owning company to place a plain yellow track tile directly on an undeveloped town hex location or upgrade a town tile of one color to a plain track tile of the next color. This closes the company and counts as the company's normal track laying step. All other normal track laying restrictions apply. Cannot be used in hexes with two small towns.

privates.name: The Hollowing
privates.rules_text: Allows the owning company to place a plain yellow track tile directly on an undeveloped town hex location or upgrade a town tile of one color to a plain track tile of the next color. This closes the company and counts as the company's normal track laying step. All other normal track laying restrictions apply. Cannot be used in hexes with two small towns.

privates.name: The Surveyors
privates.rules_text: The owning company may lay an additional yellow tile (or two for major companies beginning in Phase 3), or make one additional tile upgrade in its track laying step. All other normal track laying restrictions apply.

privates.name: The Raven Post
privates.rules_text: After running trains, the owning company receives income into its treasury equal to one half of the base value of the start and end stations from one of the trains operated. Modifications to values (for E-trains or destination tokens) do not apply. An L-train may deliver mail within a single city. A company that owns more than one Mail Contract may not use more than one on any train.

privates.name: The Courier's Guild
privates.rules_text: After running trains, the owning company receives income into its treasury equal to one half of the base value of the start and end stations from one of the trains operated. Modifications to values (for E-trains or destination tokens) do not apply. An L-train may deliver mail within a single city. privates.name: The Concord Charter
privates.rules_text: Allows the owning company to move a token from the exchange token area of its charter to the available token area, or vice versa. This company closes when its power is exercised.

privates.name: The Gilded Carriage
privates.rules_text: A 'Pullman' carriage train that can be added to another train owned by the company. It converts the train into a + train. Does not count against train limit and does not count as a train for the purposes of train ownership. Can't be sold to another company. Does not close. May include a maximum of [2 × the train size] number of towns.
